sections.h2: What is the first thing Schuylkill County needs before it records a deed?
sections.html:
A tax parcel certification stamp from the Tax Assessment Office. The county requires that stamp on deeds, mortgages, easements, rights of way, land leases and several other instruments, and it has to be completed before the Recorder of Deeds will accept the paper.

The Tax Assessment Office charges its own fee for the stamp, $20 per instrument according to the county Recorder of Deeds page. Questions about the certification go to the assessment office at 570-628-1025. This step is separate from the recording fee and from realty transfer tax, so a seller or closing agent should expect three different amounts on a Schuylkill County deed.

The county also recommends e-recording, which folds the recorder and assessment steps into one submission. That saves postage and avoids the rejection charge described below.

sections.h2: How can I pay the Schuylkill County recorder?
sections.html:
Not with a personal check. Since 2016 the office has refused personal and personal business checks. The list of what it does accept is short.

  • A check from a law firm
  • A certified bank check
  • A money order
  • Cash

Payment goes to "Schuylkill County Recorder of Deeds." If a document is rejected for any reason and was sent by mail, UPS or FedEx, the office charges a $3 rejection and return fee, and the sender must include a self-addressed stamped envelope of adequate size for the return. E-recording avoids that charge entirely.

The office also states plainly what it will not do. It does not supply forms, help prepare legal documents, notarize anything, run real estate searches, certify that a property is free and clear or give legal advice. If you need a title search, that comes from a title company or attorney.

sections.h2: How do I get a copy of a Schuylkill County deed?
sections.html:
Mail or courier a written request that gives the exact book and page number and the year of the document. The office does not search for documents and does not do genealogy research, so a request without those details cannot be filled.

For each document under 40 pages the county charges $8.50 for an uncertified copy and $10.00 for a certified copy. Enclose a self-addressed envelope of adequate size with prepaid postage. The online land records database at uslandrecords.com is the better route when you only know the owner's name, but it needs a computer, internet access and a credit card to pay for printed pages.

sections.h2: What transfer tax applies when a Schuylkill County house sells?
sections.html:
The state's realty transfer tax is 1 percent of the value of the property, and Pennsylvania's Department of Revenue makes the grantor and grantee jointly liable. County recorders collect it, often alongside a local transfer tax shared between the municipality and the school district.

The local portion depends on where the house sits in the county, from Pottsville to the smaller boroughs and townships. Ask the recorder or your closing agent for the combined percentage on your deed before closing day, so the settlement sheet matches what the office will collect.

The Department of Revenue also exempts a list of transfers, including certain transfers between family members, transfers to government units and property passing by will or intestate succession. A house inherited in Schuylkill County therefore moves to the heirs without that tax, but a sale by the heirs afterward is a new transfer.

sections.h2: Why does the Schuylkill County reassessment matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Schuylkill County's last countywide reassessment before this one dated to 1996. Property owners sued in 2018, arguing that assessments no longer met the uniformity requirement in the state constitution, and the county signed a consent decree on May 16, 2022 that committed it to a new countywide assessment.

The county's reassessment page describes a vendor, Vision Government Services, collecting property data in the field and appraising every parcel with computer-assisted mass appraisal. Its stated schedule had notices mailed on or before July 1, 2025, a formal appeal route to the Schuylkill County Board of Assessment Appeals, and new assessed values taking effect January 1, 2026.

For someone selling, the practical point is that the tax bill a buyer will pay can differ from the bill you paid in earlier years. If your assessment changed, read the notice, and ask the Tax Assessment Office how the new value applies to your parcel before you promise a buyer a tax figure.

sections.h2: What kind of county is Schuylkill, and who lives in it?
sections.html:
Schuylkill County was created on March 1, 1811 from parts of Berks and Northampton counties and takes its name from the Schuylkill River, which starts here. Pottsville is the county seat and only city. Anthracite coal was found near Pottsville in 1790, and the county sits in northeastern Pennsylvania's Coal Region. Population peaked at 235,505 in 1930 and has drifted down since, with 143,049 counted in 2020.

The county covers 783 square miles and borders eight other counties. Blue Mountain and the Appalachian Trail lie to the south, Broad Mountain crosses the middle, and the eastern edge around Tamaqua reaches the Poconos. Interstate 81, US 209 and PA 61 are among the main routes, and the county sits about 97 miles northwest of Philadelphia.

  • Population estimate, July 1, 2025: 145,085, up 1.4 percent from the 2020 base
  • Housing units, July 1, 2025: 67,679
  • Owner-occupied rate, 2020 to 2024: 76.1 percent
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020 to 2024: $153,000
  • Median gross rent, 2020 to 2024: $876
  • Median household income, 2020 to 2024: $68,313
  • Mean travel time to work: 27.3 minutes

These figures come from the Census Bureau's QuickFacts page for Schuylkill County. Median home value of $153,000 sits well below the Pike County figure of $272,600, which is the clearest sign of how different the two northeastern counties are for sellers.

sections.h2: What should a Schuylkill County seller check before the deed is signed?
sections.html:
Begin with the parcel stamp, because a deed without it cannot be recorded. Then confirm the payment method: if the closing agent hands you a personal check for the recording office, expect it to be refused.

Look at the paperwork next. A seller with a vacant or inherited house may be facing repairs, back taxes and an unclear title at the same time. Gather the prior deed, any mortgage satisfaction and the latest tax notices. If heirs share ownership, every owner of record has to sign.

Finally, ask the title company who will submit the deed. Electronic submission through the county's recommended route is quicker, and the recorder confirms the recording by book and page, which you should keep with your closing papers.

faqs.q: Does Schuylkill County accept personal checks for recording?
faqs.a: No. The recorder has refused personal and personal business checks since 2016. It accepts law firm checks, certified bank checks, money orders and cash, made payable to Schuylkill County Recorder of Deeds.

faqs.q: What is the parcel certification stamp?
faqs.a: It is a tax parcel ID certification the Tax Assessment Office applies before a deed or mortgage can be recorded. The assessment office charges $20 per instrument. Call 570-628-1025 with questions.

faqs.q: What happens if my document is rejected?
faqs.a: A mailed or courier submission that is rejected for any reason incurs a $3 rejection and return fee. You must also supply a self-addressed stamped envelope. E-recording avoids the fee.

faqs.q: How much does a copy of a recorded deed cost?
faqs.a: $8.50 for an uncertified copy and $10.00 for a certified copy, for documents under 40 pages. Send a written request with the book and page number, the year and a prepaid return envelope.

faqs.q: Is there transfer tax on an inherited house in Schuylkill County?
faqs.a: Title passing by will or intestate succession is exempt from Pennsylvania realty transfer tax. If the heirs then sell, that sale deed is taxed at the state rate of 1 percent plus any local tax, unless another exemption applies.
